title: Shocking moment Bankstown man jumps to defend Sydney nurses after their vile rant: 'I stand with them'
text:
A man in the west of Sydney has jumped to defend the two health nurses of Nueva Wales del Sur that appeared in a viral video that made shocking anti -Semitic threats against patients.
The employees of the Bankstown Hospital Ahmad ‘Rashad’ Nadir and Sarah Abu Lebdeh were filmed by the Israeli influencer Max Veifer saying that they would refuse to treat Jewish patients in their neighborhood, and Lebdeh added ‘I will kill them’.
The couple has been daring by NSW’s Nursing and Partería Council as the police investigate whether any law has been broken.
Since then, Veifer has published the complete footage and without editing of the exchange.
Bankstown locals in southwest Sydney were interrogated by the Peroratea on Thursday with a man arguing that his comments should be protected under freedom of expression.
‘They have the right free to say what they want, you know?’ He told Sky News.
‘I am with them. Yes. In any case possible.
The young man insisted that the comments of the nurses were caused by “all the children that the Jews have killed” during the Israel War in Gaza.
A Bankstown man has defended the anti -judia threats made by two NSW health nurses
Rashad Nadir (left) and Sarah Abu Lebdeh (right) of the Bankstown hospital were filmed by an influential Jew who released the video on social networks. Since then it has been eliminated
Other residents of Bankstown, the comments of the nurses “were not acceptable”, while another said “to joke like this, it is simply not fun.”
The video caused a generalized indignation of politicians and Jewish groups and both nurses have retired from their roles and apologized.
“It is the country of Palestine, not your country, you are a piece of shit,” ABU Lebdeh is heard in the clip.
“One day your time will come and you will die the most horrible death.”
“You have no idea how many (Israelis) came to this hospital and sent them to Jehannam (hell),” said Nadir, while making a gesture that slides his throat.
Freedom of expression is not explicitly mentioned in the Constitution of Australia, however, Australia has signed the UN International Pact on civil and political rights.
This document establishes the right to expression must be protected, provided that the rights and reputations of others are considered.
In that sense, Commonwealth and all states, except WA, have criminalized hate speech where there is a threat of violence or property damage.
Mohamad Abu Lebdeh (in the photo) jumped to the defense of his sister Sarah on Wednesday
The New Wales del Sur government is also looking for a new crime to “incite racial hatred”, which is expected to pass through Parliament at the end of this month.
Prime Minister Anthony Albanese in Parliament labeled this week the “comments of the nurses” unpleasant, disgusting and shameful “and said he was” clear “that a crime had been committed.
‘The NSW government has acted. They have been retired by NSW authorities. No wonder have been sent to the New Wales del Sur police for criminal investigation, ” he said.
Sarah’s brother, Mohamad Abu Lebdeh, jumped to her sister’s defense outside her house on Wednesday night, telling Daily Mail Australia that she was “barley” to make disgusting comments and what parts of the video were “cut” and “edited”.
‘Sarah wanted to be nurse all her life. She loved her work. She helps people don’t hurt them, “he said.
‘That video was a configuration. You can see what is edited. You can see jump cuts.
‘Sarah said those things but was pushed. She was barley.
Mohamad also said his sister was antagonized by Veifer.
“Sarah was born here, but has lost 70 family members in Palestine, completely annihilated,” added his brother.
She snapped. Anyone would, listen to that. To listen to those things. It’s too much, but he cut that part and made it seem that she just said that.
‘It was caused. She is a nurse and has won prizes.
Veifer broke his silence in the Sky News program of Sharri Markson on Wednesday night and issued a gloomy warning for all Australians about the emergence of anti -Semitism.
“I hope I have opened your eyes a bit to this tremendous anti -Semitism that is happening in Australia and I hope you finally start taking measures to prevent these events from happening,” he said.
‘It is not the only case. I just recorded it, right?
